transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-02
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Rivera (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Aurora PM), Priya Singh (Aurora Platform Eng), Sara Jensen (Aurora Marketplace PM)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. This is Maya from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Carlos, our solutions engineer. How's everyone today?
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: Hi Maya, thanks. All good here. Excited to go through the integration checklist.
[00:28] Priya Singh: Hey, Priya here. We'll be the technical lead from Aurora for the marketplace packaging.
[00:34] Sara Jensen: Sara on the marketplace team. I'll own listing requirements and go/no-go dates.
[00:40] Carlos Rivera: Great, quick agenda: marketplace listing artifacts, reference architecture for private/hybrid deployments, packaging (helm/terraform), and operational handoffs. We'll keep it pragmatic.

[01:05] Maya Chen: Quick context for anyone new: Redwood provides hosted API + dedicated and private deployments; for marketplace listing you can offer both hosted integration (we surface via our partner program) and a reference-arch for customers to deploy in their VPCs. We'll want to align on what Aurora is listing.
[01:27] Liam O'Connor: The primary ask from our product team is a turnkey listing that supports both an Aurora-managed SaaS integration AND a bring-your-own (BYO) private deployment reference. We need clear docs for the BYO path for enterprise customers.

[02:05] Carlos Rivera: For the BYO reference arch: typical pieces are a container image or helm chart, terraform modules for infra (VPC, subnets, routing), SSO integration notes, KMS key usage, and network peering guidance. We also include example policies for KV cache, and hints for quantized models to keep footprint small.
[02:40] Priya Singh: When you say KMS, do you support external HSM or just cloud KMS integrations?
[02:48] Carlos Rivera: Good question. Redwood supports cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and we have an HSM option for dedicated/private customers—requires additional contract. The reference doc will list both paths; for Aurora's marketplace we should call out supported KMS options so customers know pre-reqs.

[03:30] Sara Jensen: Marketplace team needs a list of required artifacts: logos, short/long description, pricing SKU mapping, support SLAs, and any certifications like SOC 2. Also we require a reference-arch doc and a vetted container image or marketplace bundle.
[03:52] Maya Chen: We'll supply assets. We have a partner asset pack template we can fill: logos, product description, sample runbook, and a tarball with helm chart and terraform module.

[04:18] Liam O'Connor: On the billing side, how will licenses be exchanged? Aurora marketplace wants metered billing via marketplace invoicing. Can Redwood produce usage reports or a metering endpoint?
[04:34] Carlos Rivera: Our hosted API emits usage records and we can provide a daily usage feed. For Dedicated/Private, it's typically license + seat/throughput agreements and manual reconciliations. I can connect you to our billing ops for the exact format.

[05:05] Priya Singh: For private deployments customers will want private networking; do you have guidance on VPC endpoints vs NAT, and if you require cross-account roles?
[05:16] Carlos Rivera: We have templates for both. Typical recommended pattern: cross-account IAM role for automation + VPC peering or PrivateLink depending on region. We'll include example TF code. Note: PrivateLink requires additional network approvals on Aurora side.

[06:00] Sara Jensen: Are there any known limitations for the marketplace image size or runtime? Our marketplace enforces limits on image size and start-up time.
[06:10] Maya Chen: Our runtime image for the reference-arch is slimmed and we publish quantized model variants; typical image is < 1.2GB compressed. Cold start time depends on model; we'll include recommended minimal instance types and tuning parameters.

[06:45] Liam O'Connor: On the security front, we need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a data flow diagram showing where customer data lives. Can Redwood provide that?
[06:56] Carlos Rivera: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2 reports and we can supply a high-level data flow and audit log examples. For Private deployments, audit logs remain in-customer control which is usually a selling point.

[07:30] Priya Singh: For SSO, do you support SAML + OIDC and SCIM provisioning?
[07:36] Carlos Rivera: Both. We have SAML, OIDC SSO and SCIM user provisioning for managed Redwood Console. For private deployments we provide SSO integration patterns.

[08:05] Sara Jensen: Good. Let's talk about the reference architecture doc: we need low-level network diagrams, example terraform modules, helm chart with values.yaml, and a short quickstart script. Can you commit to a repo link by next week?
[08:20] Maya Chen: Yes, we'll share a repo on the Redwood partners org with a README, helm, terraform, and an example docker image tag. Carlos will upload the chart.

[08:55] Carlos Rivera: Noted. On the tech details: our runtime requires ephemeral KV cache storage for sequence cache; we recommend using managed redis or our KV proxy. For high-throughput customers we provide batching knobs—these will be documented.

[09:35] Liam O'Connor: For Aurora's internal customers, latency SLOs are important. Can you publish expected p99 latency at different instance sizes?
[09:45] Carlos Rivera: We have performance profiles for our supported models; we'll include a small table in the reference-arch (p50/p95/p99 token latencies for given instance classes). There may be variation by quantization and sequence length.

[10:10] Priya Singh: About Terraform modules: do you provide source modules (GPL/Apache) or binary artifacts?
[10:19] Carlos Rivera: Source modules under an Apache2-like license. We'll provide example modules and recommended state backend patterns.

[10:40] Sara Jensen: For marketplace listing, our legal team usually needs a vendor agreement and data processing addendum. Who at Redwood handles contracts?
[10:49] Maya Chen: I'll introduce you to our partnerships legal and our sales ops. We can attach a DPA and standard partner MSA.

[11:10] Liam O'Connor: Are there any pitfalls customers see when installing the reference arch?
[11:16] Carlos Rivera: Common ones: missing IAM permissions for cross-account roles, insufficient disk for model artifacts, and network ACLs blocking model download. We'll add a preflight checklist to the repo.

[11:45] Priya Singh: Can we look at the quickstart flow for a demo? Even a short runbook of 5 steps would help.
[11:54] Carlos Rivera: Sure. Example: (1) provision VPC/subnets, (2) create IAM role + KMS key, (3) deploy terraform for infra, (4) helm install redwood-runtime --values values-prod.yaml, (5) verify healthchecks and run a sample inference. We'll paste that as a one-page runbook.

[12:30] Maya Chen: Also to highlight: for marketplace integration we typically certify the listing with a simple end-to-end validation: deploy in a sandbox Aurora account, run a test workload, and confirm metrics + logs. Would your team be open to a joint sandbox test?
[12:47] Sara Jensen: Yes, we can do a sandbox test. We'll need the repo and artifacts first.

[13:10] Liam O'Connor: On support SLAs, Aurora customers expect 24/7 for production listings. What's Redwood's support model?
[13:20] Maya Chen: For marketplace listings, Redwood's default is business hours support; for production/Dedicated customers we can offer 24/7 as add-on. We'll document support tiers in the asset pack.

[13:48] Priya Singh: For the private deployment, what are the recommended instance types for medium and large workloads?
[13:56] Carlos Rivera: We'll recommend a small/medium/large mapping (gpus or specific vm types) and provide throughput numbers. For quantized models we can run on smaller instances; we'll include a sizing guide.

[14:25] Sara Jensen: A few nitty-gritty marketplace requests: canonical product name, 1-line and 2-line descriptions, 500-char summary, icons in 512/128 px, and a CSV of SKUs for pricing tiers.
[14:40] Maya Chen: We'll populate those and use the Aurora template you shared.

[15:05] Liam O'Connor: Are there telemetry implications for Aurora customers who are strict about data residency?
[15:12] Carlos Rivera: For hosted mode, telemetry goes to Redwood's telemetry endpoints; we can provide options to redact PII and limit retention. For private deployments telemetry and logs generally stay within customer infra. We'll add those notes.

[15:40] Priya Singh: Does Redwood provide a reference terraform state example for remote state (S3/remote backend)? That would help our infra team.
[15:48] Carlos Rivera: Yes, we'll include a remote state example with recommended S3 bucket policies and encryption.

[16:15] Maya Chen: Quick clarifying question: for the marketplace SKU, do you want metered per-inference billing or subscription tiers?
[16:25] Sara Jensen: Aurora supports both. For Redwood we'd likely list both a metered hosted SKU and a reference-arch subscription listing. We'll need to know the metering granularity.

[16:46] Carlos Rivera: We meter by token for hosted API; for marketplace metering we'll map token units to marketplace units—I'll coordinate with billing ops.

[17:00] Liam O'Connor: Any compliance questionnaires we should anticipate? Some of our larger customers ask about encryption at rest, TLS in transit, and third-party subprocessors.
[17:12] Carlos Rivera: We have an FAQ and a security pack. We'll attach SOC2, encryption docs, subprocessors list, and a sample MSA.

[17:45] Priya Singh: One technical ask from our platform team: can Redwood runtime be run behind an internal ALB with client TLS? We want mTLS mutual TLS to authenticate calls.
[17:58] Carlos Rivera: Yes, the runtime supports mTLS at ingress; the helm chart exposes annotations for ALB ingress and mTLS certs. We'll add an example values-mtls.yaml.

[18:30] Maya Chen: Ok, let's surface a timeline. We propose: by 2026-10-09 Redwood shares the partner repo and asset pack; Aurora provides network diagram and legal contacts by 2026-10-09; then a joint sandbox test week of 2026-10-19. Does that work?
[18:51] Sara Jensen: That timeline looks good.

[19:10] Liam O'Connor: Last thing: are there any limitations on model cardinality or licensing for the reference arch?
[19:20] Carlos Rivera: The reference arch supports any open model we ship; for proprietary models we'll need separate licensing. We'll call that out.

[19:45] Priya Singh: Great. Could Redwood also provide a small sample benchmark script we can run in the sandbox to validate p99 latencies?
[19:53] Carlos Rivera: Yes, we'll include a small k6/locust script and sample workload.

[20:20] Maya Chen: Awesome. We'll follow up in email with links. Any other questions?
[20:27] Sara Jensen: None from me. Thanks.
[20:32] Liam O'Connor: Thanks all.
[20:35] Priya Singh: Thanks, bye.

Notes:
- Shared artifacts: Redwood partner repo (will be posted) - placeholder: https://github.com/redwood-inference/partners/auroracloud-refarch (private repo to be shared)
- Asset checklist: logos, descriptions, helm chart, terraform module, runbook, SOC2, DPA
- Possible follow-up demo: week of 2026-10-19 (sandbox)

End of transcript.
